visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a screen displaying a 3x3 grid titled 'Taiwan's Top 10 Ugliest Mascots,' featuring various local statues. A specific box containing the 'Milkfish Boy' from Tainan is highlighted with a moving selection box. This transitions to a full-screen view of the actual statue, a humanoid creature with a fish-head hood and a wide, staring expression, standing on a blue and white pedestal under a cloudy sky. (2) A young male interviewer in a black t-shirt and cap holds a microphone featuring a yellow logo. He stands on a residential street and interviews an elderly woman in a purple textured jacket. She laughs and covers her mouth, looking shyly away from the camera. The background shows a low concrete wall and parked vehicles under flat daylight. (3) The scene shifts to an outdoor area in front of a traditional Chinese temple with a red roof and elaborate carvings. The interviewer talks to a man in a grey t-shirt holding a clipboard and a smartphone, who appears to be an official. (4) An elderly man in a light green t-shirt with a marathon logo is interviewed in a medium shot. He gestures frequently with his right hand, pointing and waving to emphasize his points. A red 'Futong' delivery truck is partially visible in the background street. (5) A split-screen layout appears: the bottom half shows the interviewer in a plain room with wooden furniture, while the top half shows a female designer via a video call interface. Her face is pixelated for privacy. They engage in a conversation involving hand gestures and smiling expressions.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video investigates the origin and design philosophy behind the 'Milkfish Boy' statue in Tainan, which is infamous for being one of Taiwan's 'ugliest' mascots. It uses humor and interviews to reveal that the 'ugly' design was a strategic choice to attract media attention.
